title: Carry-forward of a picture copies the day file but not its srcDark file, which blocks publishing
description:
Reported by the Machines on Machines story-development session on CLI 5.105.0.

Related: PPY-99dcfaf6 (srcDark / .dark pairing), PPY-d92e3ba1 (Illustration step and publish gate).

Observed: when a new Story version carries a picture forward from the previous version, the light (day) file is copied but the srcDark file named by the picture is not. The publish check then refuses because the dark file is missing from the new version. The session worked around it with a byte-identical re-save of the lineage content-item-when-ai-writes-the-code-understanding-becomes-the-job-fbccd97c3948e3ce (v14 to v17). That workaround must not be needed.

Feature: Carry-forward keeps both pictures of a pair
  Scenario: A picture with a dark variant is carried into a new version
    Given a Story version whose cover has a day file and a srcDark file
    When an editor saves a new version without touching the cover
    Then the new version holds both the day file and the srcDark file
    And a publish dry run of the new version passes the picture check
  Scenario: The pair is carried as one unit
    Given a carried-forward picture whose srcDark file is missing from the source version
    When the new version is saved
    Then the save names the missing file instead of producing a version that cannot publish

Design: wherever carry-forward copies a picture, it copies every file the picture names (day and srcDark) through the same code path. No re-save workaround, no fallback.
